_about: The ONE list of part-number cases shared by scraper/sources/base.py is_part_number (Python) and
src/pipeline/partNumber.ts isPartNumber (TypeScript). tests/db/apply-enumeration.test.ts runs BOTH
over every case and misses when either disagrees with the expectation or with the other.
`accept: true` = a real part number as a vendor or a site writes it; otherwise `reason` names the
slug the token must be refused for (a refusal for another reason is a miss, not a pass).
`allow_short` cases are evaluated with the short-name opt-in (Ubiquiti sells a 'UX').
Every token was seen in the queue, on a page, or in the Cisco enumeration files (3 Sep 2026).
4 Sep 2026: the 26 numeric Cisco PIDs below are each a row in the live parts table, read
read-only from it — 12 of the assembly shape NN-NNNN..-NN (596 rows) and 14 of the six- to
eight-digit Scientific-Atlanta shape (1,029 rows). Both were refused as `quantity` until
today, and is_part_number is the ONE gate at enqueue, so 1,497 real parts could never be
fetched (docs/CISCO_GAPS.md finding 10). The second shape is a shape: 18 of those 1,029
rows are scraped numbers, not PIDs (115200 and 230400 are baud rates, 33554432 is 2^25).
They are NOT listed as accepts here — they are the measured price of the rule, and the
product-class layer, not the junk gate, is where they should be caught.
4 Sep 2026 (2nd round): three more digit-led shapes, from the planner reading its OWN
refusals — 40 queued lookups were held back. NNNN= spare orders (8201=, 8202=, 8404=,
8608=, 15216-2950=), NNNN-NN model+suffix (9800-40, 9800-80) and bare 880/890-series ISRs
(886VA, 887VA, 896VA, 897VA). Bounds were read off the 69,487-PID universe and 4,526
acquired pages, not guessed, and each is paired with the near-miss that would flip if the
widening were naive: 850VA is a REAL UPS rating inside the 8xx band (so the band alone is
not enough), 2024-10 is a year-month, 1000-4999 and 1545-1548 are real ranges, 9800-4 is
no Cisco suffix. Removing a clause of any keep must turn one of those accepts red.
